objectives: Describe Milky Way structure + the supermassive black hole Sgr A*.
Apply Hubble's tuning fork + galaxy taxonomy.
Map the cosmic web from local group to Sloan Great Wall.

slides.title: Milky Way structure + Sgr A*
slides.body:
Our home galaxy — the **Milky Way (MW)** — is a barred spiral with ~10¹¹ stars, ~30 kpc diameter, ~13.6 Gyr age (oldest stars HD 140283 + S0-2 cluster).

**Structural components**:
- **Galactic disk** (~30 kpc diameter, ~300 pc thick for thin disk + ~1 kpc for thick disk): where the Sun lives (~8.2 kpc from center, in Orion-Cygnus spur arm). Young + intermediate-age stars; gas + dust; spiral arms (Carina-Sagittarius, Scutum-Centaurus, Norma, Perseus, Local/Orion). Active star formation (~1-3 M☉/yr).
- **Galactic bulge** (~1 kpc radius): old stellar population; box-shaped (X-shaped from face-on view of the bar — peanut/boxy bulge). Mass ~10¹⁰ M☉.
- **Galactic bar** (~3-4 kpc long, ~30° tilt): central bar discovered from 2MASS + Spitzer + Gaia infrared mapping. MW is a **barred spiral (SBbc)** — not a pure unbarred spiral. ~⅔ of disk galaxies are barred.
- **Galactic halo**: spherical distribution of old metal-poor stars + globular clusters (~150 known) + dark matter (~10¹² M☉). Extends to ~100 kpc; contains satellites (LMC, SMC, Sgr dSph, ...).
- **Stellar streams** (Helmi 1999, Belokurov 2006): tidal debris from disrupted dwarf galaxies + globular clusters wrapping the halo — fossil record of past mergers. Sgr stream, GD-1, Pisces, Cetus. Gaia DR2/DR3 + photometric surveys (Pan-STARRS, DECaLS) mapped dozens. **Mark Reid** (Harvard CfA) led VLBI measurements of MW maser parallax to refine MW size (R₀ ≈ 8.15 kpc) + rotation curve.
- **Oort cloud** (~10⁴ - 10⁵ AU): hypothesized spherical reservoir of icy bodies feeding long-period comets — outer edge of solar system, ~halfway to nearest stars.
- **Kuiper belt** (~30-50 AU): trans-Neptunian disk of icy bodies (Pluto, Eris, Makemake, Haumea); studied by New Horizons.

**Sgr A*** (Sagittarius A-star, central supermassive black hole):
- Compact non-thermal radio source at galactic center, discovered Balick + Brown 1974.
- **Stellar orbits** in central parsec ('S-cluster'): **Reinhard Genzel** (MPE/Munich) + **Andrea Ghez** (UCLA) led independent decades-long monitoring with VLT + Keck adaptive optics, tracking S2/S0-2 around Sgr A*. S2 has T = 16 yr orbit, perihelion 17 light-hours. Mass → **M_BH = 4.297 × 10⁶ M☉** — direct dynamical proof of a SMBH. **2020 Physics Nobel** to Genzel + Ghez (with Penrose for theoretical BH work).
- **EHT image** (2022 May): direct horizon-scale image of Sgr A* — shadow + photon ring at ~50 μas, matching GR predictions for a Kerr BH of measured mass. After 2019 M87* image, second EHT BH portrait.
- Most quiescent of known SMBHs (Eddington ratio ~10⁻⁹) — accretes very little despite being there. Occasional X-ray + IR flares (~daily, factor 10×).

**Galactic rotation curve**: flat to large radii (Rubin + Ford 1970s for external galaxies; HI + maser + Gaia for MW) → 'missing mass' / **dark matter halo** dominating outer mass budget. Mass within 50 kpc: ~5 × 10¹¹ M☉, ~85% dark.

slides.title: Galaxy types + Hubble tuning fork
slides.body:
Edwin Hubble (1926, 1936 *Realm of the Nebulae*) introduced the **morphological classification** that still organizes extragalactic astronomy — the famous **'tuning fork' diagram**.

**Hubble sequence**:
- **Ellipticals (E0 - E7)**: smooth, featureless, mostly old red stellar populations, low gas + dust. Numerical suffix is flattening (E0 = spherical, E7 = most elongated, b/a = 0.3). Range from dwarf ellipticals (dE, 10⁶ - 10⁹ M☉) to giant ellipticals (cD; central cluster galaxies; 10¹³ M☉; M87 in Virgo cluster).
- **Lenticulars (S0)**: hybrid — disk + bulge but no spiral arms. Bridge between ellipticals + spirals.
- **Spirals (Sa, Sb, Sc)**: prominent disk + bulge + spiral arms. Sa = tight arms + large bulge; Sc = loose arms + small bulge. Most have stars + gas + dust + active star formation.
- **Barred spirals (SBa, SBb, SBc)**: spirals with central bar. MW = SBbc. The 'two prongs' of the tuning fork.
- **Irregulars (Irr / Im)**: asymmetric, often star-bursting; LMC, SMC, M82.

**De Vaucouleurs (1959) refinement**: added intermediate classifications (e.g., SAB for weakly barred), inner ring structures (r/s), outer features. Modern surveys (SDSS, Galaxy Zoo) use his system.

**Hubble's 'evolutionary' interpretation was wrong** — he thought ellipticals evolve into spirals, but the modern view is that **mergers transform spirals into ellipticals**:
- Gas-rich major merger of two spirals → strong tidal interactions + starburst → ULIRG (Arp 220, NGC 6240) → quenching of star formation → red dead elliptical.
- Dry mergers between ellipticals → more massive ellipticals.
- Minor mergers + accretion build halos + stellar streams.

**Dwarf galaxies**: most numerous — dwarf ellipticals (dE), dwarf spheroidals (dSph), dwarf irregulars (dIrr), ultra-faint dwarfs (UFDs; lowest luminosity, highest dark-matter fraction, Sextans, Draco, Reticulum II). MW has ~50+ known satellites + ~hundreds of UFDs predicted by ΛCDM ('missing satellites problem').

**Interacting + peculiar galaxies**: Arp Atlas (1966). Tidally distorted pairs + triples: Antennae (NGC 4038/4039 — merger in progress); M81/M82; Stephan's Quintet; the Whirlpool (M51) + companion. JWST sees deep structural detail of mergers.

**Active galactic nuclei (AGN)** + **quasars** (Schmidt 1963): accretion onto SMBHs → radiative output sometimes outshining the whole host galaxy. Types:
- **Seyfert galaxies** (Seyfert 1943): nearby AGN; broad + narrow emission lines.
- **Quasars** (QSOs; quasi-stellar objects): luminous high-z AGN. SDSS catalog of ~750000 quasars.
- **Radio galaxies + blazars + BL Lacs + LINERs**: subtypes by orientation + radio loudness.
- **Unified model** (Antonucci 1993; Urry + Padovani 1995): all AGN have central SMBH + accretion disk + dust torus + jets; observational differences = viewing angle + accretion rate.
- **M-σ relation** (Ferrarese + Merritt 2000; Gebhardt 2000): SMBH mass tightly correlates with bulge velocity dispersion → SMBH-galaxy coevolution.

**Star-formation history**: 'cosmic noon' at z ~ 2 — peak SFR density when universe was ~3.3 Gyr old (Madau + Dickinson 2014 review). Stars formed half their integrated mass in this epoch. Quenched/passive galaxies populate the **red sequence**; star-forming on the **blue cloud** in color-magnitude diagrams. Bimodality is fundamental.

slides.title: Large-scale structure: from Local Group to cosmic web
slides.body:
Galaxies are not randomly distributed — they cluster hierarchically into groups, clusters, superclusters, filaments, sheets, voids — the **cosmic web** of large-scale structure (LSS).

**Local Group**: ~50-100 galaxies within ~3 Mpc. Two dominant spirals: **MW** (~10¹² M☉) + **M31 Andromeda** (~1.5×10¹² M☉, 780 kpc away). M33 Triangulum. Plus ~80 dwarf satellites: LMC + SMC (MW satellites; large + small Magellanic Clouds; future minor merger ~2 Gyr from now); M32, NGC 205 (M31 satellites). MW + M31 currently approaching at ~110 km/s → **major merger in ~4.5 Gyr** → 'Milkomeda' elliptical.

**Galaxy groups + clusters**: gravitationally bound systems.
- **Groups** (10s of galaxies, ~Mpc, ~10¹³ M☉): Local Group, Sculptor Group, M81 Group.
- **Clusters** (100s-1000s of galaxies, ~5 Mpc, ~10¹⁴ - 10¹⁵ M☉): **Virgo Cluster** (~16 Mpc, ~1300 galaxies, M87 central giant elliptical + EHT BH target). **Coma Cluster** (~100 Mpc, 1000+ galaxies, Zwicky 1933 inferred dark matter from velocity dispersion). **Bullet Cluster** (1E 0657-558): cluster collision with X-ray gas vs lensing-mass offset = strong dark matter evidence.
- Clusters contain hot **intracluster medium (ICM)** at 10⁷-10⁸ K (Chandra X-ray) — provides Sunyaev-Zel'dovich (SZ) effect signal in CMB.

**Superclusters + the cosmic web**:
- **Local Supercluster** (LSC; centered on Virgo, ~33 Mpc).
- **Laniakea** (Tully + Hoffman + Pomarède + Courtois 2014; *Nature*): 'immeasurable heaven' in Hawaiian. ~520 Mly across, ~10¹⁷ M☉, including LG + Virgo + Hydra-Centaurus + Norma. Defined by **velocity flow lines** — galaxies within Laniakea flow toward the **Great Attractor** + Shapley supercluster.
- **Shapley Supercluster** (200 Mpc away in direction of Centaurus): largest concentration of galaxies in the local universe; tugs on Laniakea.
- **Cosmic web** (Bond + Kofman + Pogosyan 1996; '*kinematic theory of the cosmic web*'): galaxies trace **filaments** (1D chains) + **walls** (2D sheets) + **clusters** (3D nodes) separated by **voids** (~30-100 Mpc, mostly empty).
- **Sloan Great Wall** (Gott + Jurić 2003 from SDSS): ~1.4 Gly long wall — among the largest known structures.
- **Voids**: Boötes Void (300 Mly diameter, 280 Mly away). Eridanus Cold Spot in CMB may correlate.
- **End of homogeneity scale**: ~100 Mpc; on larger scales the universe is homogeneous + isotropic (cosmological principle holds).

**Redshift surveys** — mapping the cosmic web:
- **CfA Redshift Survey** (1985-95, Geller + Huchra): first detection of voids + walls in galaxy distribution.
- **2dFGRS** (2dF Galaxy Redshift Survey, AAO 2002, ~220000 galaxies): first detection of **baryon acoustic oscillation (BAO)** scale in clustering.
- **SDSS** (Sloan Digital Sky Survey, 2000-): 3 Mpc / 1 Mpix multifilter imager + multifiber spectrograph; **~1.5 million galaxy + 750000 quasar redshifts**; BAO confirmation (Eisenstein 2005); precision LSS cosmology.
- **BOSS / eBOSS / DESI** (2009-, 2024-): higher-z BAO + RSD measurements; current state of art.
- **Euclid** (2023 launch) + **Roman** (2027): wide-field cosmology imaging + spectroscopy.

**Baryon acoustic oscillation (BAO)**: pre-recombination, photon-baryon plasma supported sound waves; sound horizon at recombination = **150 Mpc (comoving)** = preferred separation scale for matter. After decoupling, this scale froze in as a slight excess in galaxy clustering at ~150 Mpc. Detected SDSS 2005 + 2dF; now precision **standard ruler** for cosmology. Cross-ref with cosmologist (P62) path.

**Modern cosmography**: combine LSS + CMB + weak lensing + SN Ia + BAO → constrain ΛCDM. Tensions (H₀, σ₈) hint at possible new physics — addressed in cosmologist + modern-frontier-cosmology lessons.

question.question: Estimate Sgr A*'s mass from S2/S0-2 orbital period + semi-major axis
question.goal: S2 (= S0-2) orbits Sgr A* with T ≈ 16 yr + a ≈ 970 AU. Compute the central mass + compare to 4.3×10⁶ M☉.

steps.prompt: Apply Kepler's third law (Newtonian) M = 4π²a³ / (GT²). Convert units.

steps.reveal: M ≈ 7.1×10³⁶ kg / 1.989×10³⁰ kg/M☉ ≈ 3.6×10⁶ M☉. Within ~20% of the measured 4.297×10⁶ M☉ — our quick estimate works! Genzel + Ghez tracked the full S2 orbit over decades; precise measurements give the accepted value to <1% error.

steps.prompt: What other independent evidence confirms Sgr A* is a black hole, not a dense star cluster?

acceptedAnswers: S2 perihelion at 17 light-hours = 120 AU: any star cluster of 4×10⁶ M☉ confined to this volume would be unstable + dynamically evaporated within Gyr. Plus EHT 2022 image of horizon-scale shadow.

steps.reveal: S2 reaches ~17 light-hours = 120 AU from Sgr A* at perihelion. 4×10⁶ M☉ inside that radius gives a density too high for any stable stellar cluster — dynamical evaporation + collisions would relax it within ~Myr. Must be a single compact object. EHT 2022 horizon-scale image of Sgr A* shadow at ~50 μas confirms the BH directly. Multiple lines: dynamics, compactness, EHT image, IR + X-ray flares from accretion. SMBH = best-supported astrophysical object.

question.question: Why is the Bullet Cluster (1E 0657-558) considered a 'smoking gun' for dark matter?
options: The Bullet Cluster is a collision between two galaxy clusters. X-ray observations (Chandra) trace the **hot baryonic gas** (intracluster medium, most of the visible mass) — it lags behind, decelerated by collisional drag. Gravitational lensing (Clowe 2006) maps the **total mass** — the bulk lies in two lobes that passed through each other undisturbed, offset from the gas. Most mass is collisionless + spatially separated from baryons → dark matter, not modified gravity (MOND), which would track baryons. One of the cleanest empirical distinctions between particle dark matter + alternative gravity.
question.explanation: Bullet Cluster collision: X-ray gas (most visible baryon mass) is shocked + decelerated by collisional pressure, lagging behind. Total mass (from weak gravitational lensing; Clowe et al. 2006) sits in two lobes that passed through each other undisturbed — spatially offset from gas. MOND/alternative gravity would track baryon distribution; observed offset between mass + baryons requires a non-luminous + collisionless component = dark matter. Cleanest single piece of empirical evidence for particle DM over modified gravity.

hints: What's the offset between gas + lensing mass?
What does collisionless mean for DM?
slides.workedSolution: Bullet Cluster: X-ray gas (Chandra) traces hot baryonic ICM — main visible mass, decelerated by drag during cluster collision. Lensing mass (Clowe 2006) traces total mass — passes through undeflected, in two distinct lobes separated from gas. Spatial offset between baryons + gravitational source needs a collisionless, non-luminous component. MOND can't reproduce; particle DM does. Cleanest empirical case for particle DM.

question.question: Brent Tully + collaborators (2014, Nature) defined the **Laniakea Supercluster** as our home structure by tracing **velocity flow lines** — galaxies whose proper motions converge toward the Great Attractor.
question.prompt: Walk through the methodology + implications: (1) why use velocity flows instead of just spatial proximity to define supercluster boundaries; (2) Laniakea (~520 Mly, ~10¹⁷ M☉) includes LG + Virgo + Hydra-Centaurus + Norma; the boundary is a watershed surface between attractor basins; (3) Shapley Supercluster (200 Mpc away) is even more massive — pulls on Laniakea + may itself be part of a larger structure; (4) cross-ref Sloan Great Wall + cosmic web filaments + voids (Boötes Void) + BAO at 150 Mpc; (5) how this connects to ΛCDM predictions of cosmic-web structure (Bond + Kofman + Pogosyan 1996 'cosmic web' theory).

question.question: Write the comoving baryon acoustic oscillation (BAO) sound horizon scale used as a standard ruler.
question.hint: Sound horizon at drag epoch z ~ 1060; comoving scale.

slides.workedSolution: BAO sound horizon r_s ≈ 147-150 Mpc comoving (Planck 2018: 147.05 ± 0.30 Mpc at drag epoch). Imprinted on baryon distribution as a preferred separation; detected in galaxy clustering (SDSS 2005, 2dF, BOSS, eBOSS, DESI 2024). Used as standard ruler — measure r_s at different redshifts → cosmological distances + H(z) → Ω_m, Ω_Λ, H₀, w. Tension between BAO+CMB (lower H₀) vs SH0ES Cepheids (higher H₀) → Hubble tension.

question.prompt: In ≤120 words, explain the hierarchy of galactic + intergalactic structure from Milky Way to cosmic web.
question.rubric: Mentions: MW (barred spiral SBbc, ~10¹² M☉, disk + bulge + bar + halo + Sgr A* SMBH 4.3×10⁶ M☉ Genzel/Ghez Nobel 2020) → Local Group (~50 galaxies + LG, M31, M33, dwarfs) → Virgo Cluster (~16 Mpc, 1300 galaxies, M87) → Laniakea Supercluster (520 Mly, Tully 2014 velocity-flow definition) → cosmic web (filaments + walls + voids + clusters at nodes) → end of homogeneity scale ~100 Mpc. Galaxy taxonomy (Hubble 1926 tuning fork: E + S + SB + Irr; de Vaucouleurs refinement). Sloan Great Wall + Boötes Void + Shapley Supercluster as large structures; BAO at 150 Mpc as preferred scale. Mapped by SDSS, 2dF, BOSS/eBOSS/DESI redshift surveys. ΛCDM predicts cosmic-web hierarchy from initial inflationary fluctuations grown via gravitational instability; observed structure matches predictions to high precision.
